prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1106; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the claimant reports whiplash symptoms. Claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report obtained and reviewed. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact and records the other driver's account, which matches the initial report.

Entry 3: Statements taken from two independent witnesses. Both describe the impact the same way as the insured and the other driver, and neither has any connection to the parties.

Entry 4: Photographs of both vehicles reviewed. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact speed and direction, and no prior body damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the appraiser's inspection.

Entry 5: Verified that the driver involved is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the date of loss, with no indication the damage predates the policy period.

Entry 6: Medical records requested through counsel. The reported injury fits the kind and force of a crash of this type. Prior records show a minor strain in the same area years ago that resolved fully.

Entry 7: Treatment reviewed. It followed a usual course, with care tapering as the claimant improved. Claimant later supplied a few additional details about the accident, but the core account has stayed consistent across every statement given.

Entry 8: File reviewed with supervisor. Liability appears clear on the other driver's side, and the claim will proceed to evaluation of the injury component through counsel.
